intro.title: Merge a font family into one file, and add the Gulf currency symbols
intro.lede: Upload the weights, choose what to add, and download one file that installs with a single click. Saudi Riyal, UAE Dirham and Omani Rial in their official artwork, with typed shortcuts that work inside any application.
intro.privacy: Your font never leaves your device. Everything runs inside the browser, and the page is technically forbidden from sending any file to any server. How?
s1.title: Upload
s1.dropSub: ttf or otf — processed on your machine, never uploaded
s1.routeMerge: A static family — full route: merge plus symbols.
s1.routeSymbols: This is a variable font. Merging is not possible with one, so the route here is symbols only, with the symbol's width pinned across every design axis.
s1.warnMixedUpem: Files use different em units ({d}) — they cannot be combined as they are.
s1.warnItalicsNoArabic: The italics have no Arabic while the uprights carry {d} Arabic letters. It can be copied across.
s1.warnCff2: Variable CFF2 file: adding glyphs to one is not supported here.
s1.warnNames: {n} file(s) carry the common name-table bug (nameID 2 says Regular for every weight) — the build fixes it.
s1.unreadable: {n} file(s) could not be read: not valid fonts.
s1.tierFull: Comfortable size — full route with live preview of every weight.
s1.tierMedium: Medium files — build with a progress bar, live preview of three weights.
s1.tierHeavy: Large files — sequential build, no live preview. A self-test page is provided instead.
s1.tierReject: These files are larger than a browser can handle ({d}). Saving a font needs five to eight times its size in memory.
s1.localToolsWhy: The same scripts run on your machine with no size ceiling.
s2.title: Acknowledgement
s2.licenseFound: The licence, as written inside the file itself:
s2.licenseNone: No licence record inside the file. That does not mean it is unlicensed — check where the font came from.
s2.oflNotice: SIL Open Font License. This file declares no Reserved Font Name, so clause 3 does not apply and renaming is not required — it stays a useful option for avoiding a name clash with an installed copy.
s2.blocked: This file may not be modified. The foundry set the Restricted License Embedding bit in OS/2.fsType inside the font — the clearest possible signal against modification, and it comes from the file itself rather than from our guesswork.
s2.point1: I confirm I hold the right to modify this font under its licence.
s2.point2: The tool processes locally and neither receives nor stores any file.
s2.point3: The result is my responsibility, with no warranty of fitness for any commercial use.
s2.agree: I accept the terms of use
s2.agreeSub: Full text in the terms of use.
s3.title: Options
s3.symbolNote: Artwork comes from the issuing authorities and is added unchanged.
s3.shortcutsSub: Type the shortcut and it becomes the symbol. The rules are guarded: words containing the shortcut inside them are left alone.
s3.graftSub: The italics in this family have no Arabic, so Arabic text falls back to a system font. Copying from the matching upright fixes it, and the Arabic stays upright as convention has it.
s3.renameHintFree: Optional. Leave empty to keep the original name.
s3.formatAuto: Automatic — follows the source outline type
s3.formatTtc: ttc — installs on both Windows and macOS
s3.formatOtc: otc — macOS and Adobe, outlines untouched
s3.formatHintTtc: Converts CFF outlines to TrueType. Windows has no Install action for otc at all, and this is the fix.
s3.formatHintOtc: Outlines stay identical to the source. Will not install on Windows.
s3.formatHintSingle: No collection file — for apps that handle collections poorly.
s3.woff2Sub: Browsers cannot read collection files at all, so the web bundle is compressed standalone files plus a ready-made CSS file.
s3.woff2Unavailable: Unavailable: the brotli library did not load in this session.
s3.versionHint: Raise it on every build. Operating systems and Adobe cache fonts by PostScript name, and without a bump you may be served the old one.
s4.title: Preview and verification
s4.acrossWeightsWhy: The symbol is one fixed drawing at every weight — it is an official mark with a single approved shape, not a letter redrawn per weight. Look at it here before you download.
s4.reportWhy: Compared against your original file, not against an absolute standard. Whatever was missing in the source stays missing and is not counted against us — red means new breakage the build caused.
s4.findCodepointsLost: {n} codepoint(s) present in the source were lost: {d}
s4.findAdvanceNew: {n} glyph(s) disagree between hmtx and the charstring — shows as dead space in Adobe apps
s4.findAdvancePre: {n} advance mismatch(es) were already in the source — not ours
s4.shapingFired: shortcuts actually fire in this browser: {a} of {b}
s4.shapingHow: Measured as the width difference with calt on and off — that is your browser's own shaping engine.
s4.timeout: The build passed {n} seconds and was stopped. The file is beyond what a browser can do — try the local tools.
s4.noPreview: Live preview is off at this size. Download the self-test page from the next step to check the file.
s5.title: Download
s5.conflict: Remove the old copy first. The new file carries the same PostScript name ({d}), and operating systems cache fonts by that name — so you may keep being served the old font no matter what you do. Remove, install, then restart the application.
s5.conflictRenamed: Renamed, so there is no clash with any installed copy.
s5.stepsWindows: Right-click the file and choose Install for all users.|Remove any older copy of the same font first.|Restart the application — apps read fonts at launch.
s5.stepsMac: Double-click the file and choose Install Font.|Remove the old copy from Font Book first.|Restart the application.
s5.stepsAdobe: Install the file as your system does.|Quit every Adobe application.|Delete the AdobeFnt*.lst files from the cache folder.|Reopen the app. Most "the font doesn't show up" reports are this cache.
s5.stepsLinux: Copy the file into ~/.local/share/fonts/.|Run fc-cache -f.|Restart the application.
s5.windowsOtcWarning: You chose otc — Windows shows no Install action for that format at all. Go back and choose ttc.
s5.selftestBody: One page with the font embedded whole. If the symbol shows there, the file is fine and the problem is installation or the app — which saves an entire round of guessing.
s5.codepointNote: These currency codepoints are new in Unicode, so your system's character map will not list them — it reads the OS Unicode database, not the font. In Adobe: Type ▸ Glyphs with Show: Entire Font reads the font directly and shows them at the end.

engine.ready: Engine ready — fontTools {v}, inside your browser
engine.severed: Network access inside the engine is now revoked, and verified.
engine.notSevered: The engine could not revoke network access in this browser; the CSP is the only barrier.
s3.renameNeedsAscii: Add at least one Latin letter or digit. The PostScript name inside the font accepts only ASCII by OpenType spec, and a suffix without any would leave the reserved name unchanged — so the licence condition would not actually be met.
s2.oflRfnNotice: SIL Open Font License with a reserved name: {d}. Clause 3 forbids any modified version from using that name without explicit written permission from the copyright holder, so renaming is required.
s3.renameHintRfn: Required: this file reserves the name {d}, and OFL clause 3 forbids using it in a modified version.
s3.renameHintOflNoRfn: Optional. The licence is the OFL, but the file reserves no name, so nothing obliges you — avoiding a name clash is still a good reason.
s3.renameOverrideWhy: Clause 3 carves out the exception itself: "unless explicit written permission is granted by the corresponding Copyright Holder". Tick this if you hold that permission, or if the reserved-name detection got it wrong.
s3.renameOverrideOn: The reserved name {d} will stay in the file unchanged. You are asserting you may do that, and it is on you. Practical warning too: an identical name means the operating system may keep serving you the old copy from its cache.
about.title: About
about.by: Built by {d} — open source under the MIT licence.
about.invite: Review, suggestions and improvements are welcome on GitHub.
about.thirdParty: The code is MIT. The currency artwork comes from the issuing authorities and the interface font Readex Pro is under the OFL — details in NOTICE in the repository.
s3.addCurrencySub: For a currency Unicode has not encoded a symbol for yet. Upload its official artwork, pick a codepoint and a shortcut.
s3.customLegal: The artwork must come from the issuing authority. Currency symbols are state marks: do not trace one from a screenshot and do not draw it from memory — an approximation is wrong. Use of the mark is governed by that authority's rules, not by this tool's licence, and the responsibility is yours.
s3.customSvgNeed: The file needs a viewBox attribute so the symbol can be scaled to cap height.
s3.customCpHintPua: Inside the Private Use Area (U+E000–U+F8FF) — the right home for a symbol Unicode has not encoded. Be aware that these codepoints mean nothing outside a font that defines them, so do not expect copy-paste to carry them into another program.
s3.customCpHintCurrency: Inside the Currency Symbols block. Unicode reserves these for encoded currencies, and one may later be assigned to a different currency, putting your font at odds with the standard. Use the Private Use Area unless this codepoint really is the assigned one.
s3.customCpHintOther: Outside the safe areas. If this codepoint is used in your font the symbol will be refused, to protect your existing glyphs.
s3.customBadCp: Not a valid codepoint. Write it in hexadecimal, e.g. E000.
s3.customDupCp: That codepoint is already used by another currency you added.
err.cpTaken: Codepoint U+{d} is already used in your font — adding it would have replaced a real character.
err.cpSurrogate: That codepoint is reserved and cannot carry a character.
err.svgNoViewbox: The artwork file has no viewBox.
skill.title: The skill itself — for Claude or the command line
skill.body: The same engine that runs on this page is available as a Claude skill and as a command-line tool with no size ceiling. The archive is assembled in your browser, now, from this repository's own files.
skill.installCode: Unzip into ~/.claude/skills/arabic-font-merge, then pip install fonttools brotli uharfbuzz. In the Claude apps, upload the zip as a skill.
